# uSDT

`uSDT` fits hierarchical signal detection theory models to paired
awareness and influence measures. It compares mean sensitivities,
estimates their latent association and tests influence sensitivity at
zero awareness sensitivity. Development features include Bayesian
estimation with brms and Bayes factors, and study planning for power,
precision, cost and detectable effects.

## Documentation

The package website is at **<https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/>**
and documents the version on CRAN. It contains:

- [Getting
  started](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/articles/uSDT-tutorial.html),
  a tutorial that walks through the whole workflow with real data, from
  two trial-level data frames to the three hypotheses.
- [Reference](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/reference/index.html),
  the help page of every function.
- [Changelog](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/news/index.html),
  the changes in each release.

The development version from GitHub has its own website at
**<https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/>**, with two additional
tutorials:

- [Bayesian
  estimation](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/articles/uSDT-bayesian.html),
  the same analysis with priors, posterior summaries and Bayes factors.
- [Planning a uSDT
  study](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/articles/uSDT-power.html),
  power analysis and the choice of subjects and trials, with the
  tutorial data as a pilot study.

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("uSDT")
```

Or install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("RicardoReySaez/uSDT@dev")
```

The development version installs `brms`. Bayesian fitting also needs a
C++ toolchain and either rstan with `BH` and `RcppEigen`, or cmdstanr
with CmdStan.

## Example: Vadillo et al. data

The examples below use the development API.

The package includes the two trial-level data frames from Experiment 2
of Vadillo et al. (2025): `vadillo_awareness` for the awareness task and
`vadillo_cuing` for the influence task.

``` r

library(uSDT)

data(vadillo_awareness)
data(vadillo_cuing)

d <- usdt_data_tasks(
  awareness = vadillo_awareness,
  influence = vadillo_cuing,
  subject_col = "subj",
  condition_col = "condition",
  condition_levels = c(signal = "old", noise = "new"),
  response_col = list(awareness = "judged.old", influence = "rt"),
  response_levels = list(
    awareness = c(signal = 1, noise = 0),
    influence = c(signal = "faster", noise = "slower")
  ),
  dichotomize = list(awareness = FALSE, influence = TRUE)
)

fit <- hsdt(d)
summary(fit)

# The same model with brms, and Bayes factors for the three hypotheses
fit_bayes <- hsdt(d, estimation = "bayesian")
summary(fit_bayes)
usdt_bf(fit_bayes)
```

Column, level and format arguments take a shared value or task-specific
values as `list(awareness = ..., influence = ...)`.

The source data are from Vadillo, Malejka, and Shanks (2025), *Mapping
the reliability multiverse of contextual cuing*,
[doi:10.1037/xlm0001410](https://doi.org/10.1037/xlm0001410).

# Package index

## Prepare the data

Build paired task data, dichotomize continuous responses and count
trials for custom binomial models.

- [`usdt_data_tasks()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_data.md)
  [`usdt_data_long()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_data.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_data>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_data.md)
  : Prepare data for hierarchical SDT models
- [`meyen_split()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/meyen_split.md)
  : Dichotomize response times into binary choices
- [`usdt_aggregate()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_aggregate.md)
  : Count binary responses by group

## Estimate descriptive SDT measures

Calculate subject-level SDT quantities without fitting a model.

- [`sdt_moments()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/sdt_moments.md)
  : Signal detection measures for each subject

## Fit the hierarchical model

Estimate the paired sensitivities with a binomial probit mixed model.

- [`hsdt()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/hsdt.md)
  [`summary(`*`<hsdt>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/hsdt.md)
  [`print(`*`<hsdt>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/hsdt.md)
  : Fit a hierarchical signal detection theory model

## Specify the Bayesian priors

Choose the prior distributions of the Bayesian model and check what they
imply.

- [`usdt_priors()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_priors.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_priors>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_priors.md)
  : Priors for the Bayesian hierarchical SDT model
- [`plot(`*`<usdt_priors>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot.usdt_priors.md)
  : Prior predictive check for the Bayesian hierarchical SDT model

## Test hypotheses and bootstrap uncertainty

sensitivity_diff() compares mean sensitivities. Latent_cor() estimates
their latent correlation. Latent_regression() estimates the intercept
and slope. usdt_tests() collects all three hypotheses. usdt_boot() adds
parametric bootstrap inference to a fitted uSDT model.
usdt_equivalence() tests equivalence, non-inferiority and minimal-effect
hypotheses about the same quantities.

- [`usdt_tests()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_hypotheses.md)
  [`sensitivity_diff()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_hypotheses.md)
  [`latent_cor()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_hypotheses.md)
  [`latent_regression()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_hypotheses.md)
  : Test the three core hypotheses of a hierarchical SDT model
- [`usdt_boot()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_boot.md)
  : Parametric bootstrap intervals for hierarchical SDT models
- [`usdt_equivalence()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_equivalence.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_equivalence>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_equivalence.md)
  : Equivalence, non-inferiority and minimal-effect tests

## Bayes factors

Test point, directional and interval hypotheses about the difference,
correlation and latent regression of a Bayesian fit, and plot their
prior and posterior.

- [`usdt_bf()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_bf.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_bf>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_bf.md)
  : Bayes factors for the hypotheses of a Bayesian hierarchical SDT
  model
- [`plot(`*`<usdt_bf>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot.usdt_bf.md)
  : Plot the prior and posterior of tested quantities

## Plan a study

Describe the population a planned study samples from, in either
parameterization of the model or from the estimates of a pilot study.
Compute the power of the three hypotheses for a number of subjects and
of trials per task. Choose the subjects and trials at the lowest cost
and find the smallest effect a design detects.

- [`usdt_population()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_population.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_population>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_population.md)
  [`update(`*`<usdt_population>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_population.md)
  : Population values for planning a uSDT study
- [`usdt_power()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_power.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_power>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_power.md)
  [`summary(`*`<usdt_power>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_power.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.usdt_power>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_power.md)
  : Power of a planned uSDT study
- [`usdt_plan()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_plan.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_plan>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_plan.md)
  : Plan the subjects and trials of a uSDT study
- [`usdt_mdes()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_mdes.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_mdes>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_mdes.md)
  : Smallest effect a uSDT study detects
- [`plot(`*`<usdt_population>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot_power.md)
  [`plot(`*`<usdt_power>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot_power.md)
  [`plot(`*`<usdt_mdes>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot_power.md)
  [`plot(`*`<usdt_plan>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot_power.md)
  : Plot a population, its power, its smallest effects or a plan

## Visualize the fit and estimate reliability

Compare observed and fitted estimates and quantify measurement
reliability.

- [`plot(`*`<hsdt>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/plot.hsdt.md)
  : Diagnostic and analytical plots for hierarchical SDT models
- [`usdt_reliability()`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_reliability.md)
  [`summary(`*`<usdt_reliability>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_reliability.md)
  [`print(`*`<usdt_reliability>`*`)`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/usdt_reliability.md)
  : Reliability of awareness and influence task measures

## Example datasets

Trial-level data from Experiment 2 of Vadillo, Malejka and Shanks
(2025).

- [`vadillo_awareness`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/vadillo_awareness.md)
  : Awareness data from a probabilistic cuing experiment
- [`vadillo_cuing`](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/reference/vadillo_cuing.md)
  : Cuing data from a probabilistic cuing experiment

# Articles

### Tutorials

- [Fitting a hierarchical SDT
  model](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/articles/uSDT-tutorial.md):

  A complete pass over the uSDT workflow, from two trial-level data
  frames to the three hypotheses of the unconscious-processing design,
  using the contextual cuing data of Vadillo, Malejka and Shanks (2025).

- [Bayesian estimation with
  uSDT](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/articles/uSDT-bayesian.md):

  The Bayesian side of uSDT on the contextual cuing data of the
  tutorial: priors, a brms fit of the hierarchical SDT model, the three
  hypotheses, Bayes factors, the plots and the latent regression
  parameterization.

- [Planning a uSDT
  study](https://ricardoreysaez.github.io/uSDT/dev/articles/uSDT-power.md):

  How many subjects, and how many trials in each task? The power of the
  three hypotheses, the cheapest design that reaches it, the smallest
  effect a design detects and a check by simulation, with the contextual
  cuing data of Vadillo, Malejka and Shanks (2025) as a pilot study.
